prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (ideology-neutral; no parties or individuals named)

Economy and public finances
- Cut the deficit via an emergency budget, an independent Office for Budget Responsibility, and departmental savings; freeze most public-sector pay for a year (excluding the lowest paid); review bringing forward the state pension age to 66; reduce senior public pensions; cut ministerial pay; reduce the number of MPs; shrink Whitehall and quango costs.
- Modify National Insurance plans by raising thresholds to reduce costs for most employees and employers, funded by in-year savings.
- Lower and simplify business taxes (headline corporation tax to 25%, small companies to 20%), create a five‑year corporate tax roadmap, simplify rules for multinationals and intellectual property, and establish an Office of Tax Simplification.
- Promote exports, R&D and STEM; refocus R&D tax credits on hi‑tech SMEs; multi‑year science budgets; sector-focused trade support.
- Encourage saving: restore earnings link for the basic state pension; support auto‑enrolment; remove the effective annuity requirement at 75; reform consumer finance with a new protection agency and free national financial advice.
- Jobs and skills: a single Work Programme with payment‑by‑results providers; reassess incapacity claims; stronger conditionality; NI holiday for the first 10 hires in new firms; 400,000 placements and apprenticeships; free colleges from central control; more university places and careful HE funding reform.

Infrastructure and regional growth
- High Speed Rail from London/Heathrow to Birmingham, Manchester and Leeds; oppose additional runways at Heathrow, Stansted and Gatwick; rail franchise reform; national EV charging network; “Fair Fuel Stabiliser” consultation.
- Superfast broadband via infrastructure access (and potential licence fee use); local enterprise partnerships; business‑rate incentives.

Financial system
- Bank levy; prudential supervision under the central bank; constraints on risky trading and bonuses; promote competition; expand affordable SME credit.

Public services and society
- Expand choice and transparency in the NHS; GP‑led commissioning; reduce admin costs; 24/7 urgent care; Cancer Drug Fund; personal budgets for long‑term conditions; stronger public health focus and “health premium.”
- Families: end the couple penalty in tax credits; recognise couples in the tax system; two‑year council tax freeze; protect key pensioner benefits; extend flexible working and shared parental leave; refocus Sure Start and add health visitors; curb marketing to children.
- Schools: tougher discipline; attract career‑changers and veterans into teaching; phonics and age‑6 reading check; more rigorous curricula and exams; technical academies; expand academies/free schools; pupil premium; protect special schools; sharper Ofsted focus.
- Crime and justice: tougher licensing and pricing to curb binge drinking; early interventions; custodial presumption for knife crime; elected local police commissioners; publish local crime data monthly; Border Police Force; rehabilitation paid by results; stronger drug treatment orders.

Politics, transparency and localism
- Recall for MPs; tighter lobbying and donations rules; public petitions to trigger debates and a public reading stage for bills; equalised constituencies; more parliamentary autonomy; civil service reform.
- Open data rights; publish spending, contracts, and senior pay; cut non‑essential quangos; procurement reform.
- “Open source” planning led by neighbourhoods; abolish regional targets; first‑time buyer stamp duty relief; community rights to buy/run services; local referendums and vetoes on high council tax; more elected city mayors.

Civil liberties and the Union
- Scrap ID cards and major national databases; UK Bill of Rights; reform libel laws; limit surveillance and powers of entry; proportionate DNA retention; scale back vetting and barring.
- Implement Scottish finance/devolution reforms; permit a Welsh powers referendum; support Northern Ireland institutions; address England‑only voting fairness.

Environment and energy
- Cut emissions 80% by 2050; 10% cut in central government emissions in year one; smart grid/meters; emissions performance standards; new nuclear (without subsidy); four CCS plants; offshore grid and marine parks; district heating; incentives for local and small‑scale generation; energy regulator reform; diversify gas and storage.
- Green Deal for home efficiency; clearer bills and appliance standards.
- Protect habitats and species; reform fisheries; marine zones; tree planting; anti‑illegal logging law; higher animal welfare; honest food labelling; supermarket ombudsman; waste‑reduction incentives; water and flood‑resilience reforms.

Foreign policy, defence and aid
- National Security Council; strategic defence review; support mission in Afghanistan; renew nuclear deterrent; defence procurement and MOD reform; enhance support for service personnel, families and veterans.
- Active global engagement; uphold human rights; strengthen alliances; support EU enlargement with safeguards; referendum lock on any future EU power transfers; sovereignty legislation; seek repatriation of specific competences.
- Maintain aid at 0.7% of national income by 2013 with legislation; full transparency and payment by results; focus on the poorest and on malaria; climate‑smart aid; support trade and wealth‑creation institutions; new stabilisation and reconstruction capacity.
</text>
